# Effect-size candidates (not significant) {#sec-effect-size} Genes and pathways with a biologically sized Cre effect that do not reach padj < 0.05, laid out with every line of evidence so the choice of what to report can be made on the evidence. ## Criteria and liver APOE biology The main model finds no gene at padj < 0.05, which is expected with three batch-control GFP mice. This chapter collects every gene and pathway with a Cre-vs-GFP effect of at least 1.5-fold that does **not** reach significance. Each one comes with every line of evidence this dataset offers, so you can judge it. Nothing here is an FDR-controlled discovery. The list is hypothesis-generating: candidates for a justified write-up and for qPCR. The criteria select the list; the evidence columns only describe it, and no gene is dropped for failing one. **Criteria** (all parameters below): | Criterion | Default | Why | |---|---|---| | Effect size | \|log2FC\| ≥ log2(1.5) in the main model | the conventional minimum meaningful fold change; main model = batch-corrected, all controls | | Expression | baseMean ≥ 20 | below this a 1.5-fold change is a handful of reads | | Not significant | padj ≥ 0.05 | significant genes are already in chapter 4 | | Direction holds | same sign in the 2025-10-only test and in every leave-one-GFP-out refit | the sign cannot rest on one control mouse or on the run correction | **Biological context.** The switch replaces apoE4 with apoE2 on hepatocyte lipoproteins. The gene sets below follow from that biology: - receptor-mediated lipoprotein clearance (apoE2 binds LDLR poorly); - hepatocyte cholesterol sensing (SREBP2) and efflux; - VLDL assembly and triglyceride handling; - fatty-acid oxidation and synthesis; - bile acids; - ceramides (raised in these mice's plasma lipidomics); - acute-phase / ER-stress responses. Three sets were added *after* looking at this dataset: OXPHOS, the urea cycle (Ass1 / Asl) and interferon-γ response (Irgm / Gbp genes). They are kept as a separate family and cannot be presented as pre-specified. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Effect-size candidates: genes / pathways whose Cre-vs-GFP effect is as large as a biologically # meaningful change but that do not reach padj < PADJ_CUT. Every threshold is here so it can be # changed; nothing below decides what is biologically important. ES_LFC <- log2(1.5) # |batch-corrected log2FC| >= 1.5-fold (main model, unshrunk MLE) ES_MIN_MEAN <- 20 # baseMean floor: below this a 1.5-fold change is a few reads ES_CONSISTENT <- TRUE # also require the same sign in the 2025-10-only test and in every # leave-one-GFP-out refit (direction cannot hinge on one control) ES_GSEA_FDR <- 0.25 # exploratory GSEA cut-off recommended by Subramanian et al. 2005 ES_NES <- 1.5 # |NES| floor for genome-wide near-miss GO terms ES_SHOW_OTHER <- 15 # candidates outside the APOE-liver sets shown in the figure (top |LFC|) # Liver APOE biology. An E4 -> E2 switch in hepatocytes changes the apoE on hepatic lipoproteins: # apoE2 binds the LDL receptor poorly (remnant clearance, hepatocyte cholesterol delivery and so # SREBP2 signalling), and apoE isoform changes VLDL-triglyceride secretion, hepatic lipid handling # and inflammation (Mahley & Rall 2000; Mahley 2016). Plasma lipids, ceramides and triglycerides # rose in these mice (lipidomics). "a priori" sets follow from that biology; "this data" sets were # picked after seeing this dataset (OXPHOS and immune GSEA, Ass1 / Asl / Irgm2 genes) and cannot be # claimed as pre-specified. APOE_LIVER_SETS <- tribble( ~set, ~go, ~basis, "Lipoprotein assembly / VLDL secretion", "GO:0034377", "a priori", "Lipoprotein clearance (LDLR / LRP1)", "GO:0034381", "a priori", "Cholesterol biosynthesis (SREBP2)", "GO:0006695", "a priori", "Cholesterol efflux", "GO:0033344", "a priori", "Bile acid metabolism", "GO:0008206", "a priori", "Fatty acid beta-oxidation (PPARa)", "GO:0006635", "a priori", "Fatty acid synthesis (SREBP1c)", "GO:0006633", "a priori", "Triglyceride metabolism", "GO:0006641", "a priori", "Ceramide biosynthesis", "GO:0046513", "a priori", "Acute-phase response", "GO:0006953", "a priori", "ER unfolded protein response", "GO:0030968", "a priori", "OXPHOS (nuclear)", "GO:0006119", "this data", "Urea cycle", "GO:0000050", "this data", "Response to interferon-gamma", "GO:0034341", "this data") ``` ::: ## Genes **Evidence per gene** (columns `ev_*` in `csv/deseq2/effect_size_candidates.csv`): - **p < 0.05, main model** / **p < 0.05, 2025-10 only**: nominal (unadjusted) p values in the batch-corrected model and in the run-free 2025-10-only model. - **Dose**: within the Cre mice only, the slope of expression on each mouse's liver E2 allelic fraction, in the same direction as the Cre effect (and p < 0.05). Batch cannot drive a within-group gradient, but the E2 range is narrow (about 0.87–0.96). - **Germline E2 vs E4**: same direction as EFAD E2/E2 vs E4/E4 liver. Those mice are run-clean, but they differ from the switch in colony, sex, age and lifelong exposure. Disagreement is informative, not disqualifying: the switch is acute and adult-onset. - **Liver-specific**: the brain effect is opposite in sign or less than half the liver effect. - **Not a replicate false positive**: the gene does not differ between the two runs of the same mouse. - **Not tracking library quality**: |r| < 0.6 with STAR uniquely-mapped % within the Cre mice. **Calibration.** The brain column of the table below is the same filter applied where the switch should do nothing. The ratio of brain to liver counts is a rough guide to how many liver candidates could be noise. Brain has one fewer batch-control GFP mouse (B13 excluded), which makes brain somewhat noisier. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} apoe_sets <- APOE_LIVER_SETS |> mutate(genes = map2(go, set, \(g, s) { x <- go_members(g) if (str_detect(s, "OXPHOS")) setdiff(x, mt_ids) else x })) # one label per gene for the figures: its most specific (smallest) set; every membership is kept # in apoe_sets_all apoe_member <- apoe_sets |> mutate(n = lengths(genes)) |> dplyr::select(set, basis, n, genes) |> unnest(genes) |> dplyr::rename(ensemblID = genes) |> arrange(n) |> group_by(ensemblID) |> mutate(apoe_sets_all = paste(set, collapse = "; ")) |> slice(1) |> ungroup() |> dplyr::select(-n) # dose-response per gene (summary in VALIDITY CHECKS): Cre mice only, ~ sex + E2 fraction dose_gene_res <- function(tissue) { cm <- aav_meta(tissue) |> rownames_to_column("sample") |> dplyr::filter(treatment == "Cre", run == CRE_RUN) |> left_join(e2_by_mouse, by = "mouse_id") |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(e2_frac)) |> column_to_rownames("sample") |> mutate(e2_frac_c = as.numeric(scale(e2_frac))) DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(geneCounts[gene_qc[[tissue]]$keep, rownames(cm)], cm, ~ sex + e2_frac_c) |> norm_dds() |> DESeq(quiet = TRUE) |> results(name = "e2_frac_c") } res_col <- function(r, ids, col) as.data.frame(r)[ids, col] # one row per gene: main effect + every line of evidence. `other` = the other tissue's main fit # (liver-specific check for liver; for brain it is the liver fit, shown for symmetry). es_table <- function(tissue) { f <- fits$fit[[match(tissue, fits$tissue)]] other <- fits$fit[[match(setdiff(TISSUES, tissue), fits$tissue)]]$res germ <- germline$res[[which(germline$tissue == tissue & germline$a == "E2" & germline$b == "E4")]] dose <- dose_gene_res(tissue) loo <- map(f$loo, \(l) l$res$log2FoldChange) |> purrr::reduce(cbind) if (is.null(dim(loo))) loo <- matrix(loo, ncol = 1) libq <- cand_genes_all |> dplyr::filter(tissue == !!tissue) |> dplyr::select(ensemblID, r_with_lib_quality, replicate_fp) as_tibble(as.data.frame(f$res), rownames = "ensemblID") |> transmute(tissue = tissue, ensemblID, baseMean, log2FC = log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue, padj, ci_lo = log2FC - 1.96 * lfcSE, ci_hi = log2FC + 1.96 * lfcSE, log2FC_shrunk = f$resLFC$log2FoldChange, loo_same_sign = rowSums(sign(loo) == sign(log2FC)) == ncol(loo), loo_min_abs_lfc = apply(abs(loo), 1, min), run_offset_log2 = f$offset[ensemblID]) |> mutate(log2FC_oct = res_col(f$within, ensemblID, "log2FoldChange"), p_oct = res_col(f$within, ensemblID, "pvalue"), dose_lfc_per_sd = res_col(dose, ensemblID, "log2FoldChange"), p_dose = res_col(dose, ensemblID, "pvalue"), log2FC_germline_E2vsE4 = res_col(germ, ensemblID, "log2FoldChange"), p_germline = res_col(germ, ensemblID, "pvalue"), log2FC_other_tissue = res_col(other, ensemblID, "log2FoldChange")) |> left_join(libq, by = "ensemblID") |> left_join(dplyr::select(id2name, ensemblID, Symbol), by = "ensemblID") |> left_join(dplyr::select(apoe_member, ensemblID, apoe_set = set, apoe_basis = basis, apoe_sets_all), by = "ensemblID") |> mutate( # the criteria (what puts a gene on the list) meets_effect = abs(log2FC) >= ES_LFC & baseMean >= ES_MIN_MEAN, not_sig = is.na(padj) | padj >= PADJ_CUT, consistent = sign(log2FC_oct) == sign(log2FC) & loo_same_sign, candidate = meets_effect & not_sig & (consistent | !ES_CONSISTENT), # the evidence (reported, never used to drop a gene) ev_nominal_main = pvalue < 0.05, # NA = Cook's outlier, no p value ev_nominal_oct = p_oct < 0.05, ev_dose_same_sign = sign(dose_lfc_per_sd) == sign(log2FC), ev_dose_nominal = ev_dose_same_sign & p_dose < 0.05, ev_germline_E2_like = sign(log2FC_germline_E2vsE4) == sign(log2FC), ev_germline_nominal = ev_germline_E2_like & p_germline < 0.05, # liver-specific: the switch acts in hepatocytes; a gene that moves as much in brain looks # like genetic background or a systemic / technical effect ev_tissue_specific = is.na(log2FC_other_tissue) | sign(log2FC_other_tissue) != sign(log2FC) | abs(log2FC_other_tissue) < abs(log2FC) / 2, ev_not_replicate_fp = !replicate_fp %in% TRUE, ev_not_lib_quality = is.na(r_with_lib_quality) | abs(r_with_lib_quality) < 0.6) |> relocate(tissue, ensemblID, Symbol, apoe_set, apoe_basis) } es_by_tissue <- map(set_names(TISSUES), es_table) es_all <- es_by_tissue$Liver es_genes <- es_all |> dplyr::filter(candidate) |> arrange(pvalue) write_csv(bind_rows(es_by_tissue), file.path(CSV_DIR, "deseq2", "effect_size_all_genes.csv")) write_csv(bind_rows(es_by_tissue) |> dplyr::filter(candidate) |> arrange(tissue, pvalue), file.path(CSV_DIR, "deseq2", "effect_size_candidates.csv")) # How the list is built, step by step. Brain is the negative control: the AAV-TBG switch acts in # hepatocytes, so the brain count is roughly what the same filter lets through without a switch. es_funnel <- imap(es_by_tissue, \(d, t) { cand <- dplyr::filter(d, candidate) tibble(tissue = t, step = c("tested genes", sprintf("|log2FC| >= %.2f and baseMean >= %d", ES_LFC, ES_MIN_MEAN), sprintf("... and padj >= %.2f (not significant)", PADJ_CUT), "... and same sign in 2025-10-only and every leave-one-out", "... of which nominal p < 0.05 (main model)", "... of which in an APOE-liver set"), n = c(sum(!is.na(d$pvalue)), sum(d$meets_effect, na.rm = TRUE), sum(d$meets_effect & d$not_sig, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(cand), sum(cand$ev_nominal_main, na.rm = TRUE), sum(!is.na(cand$apoe_set)))) }) |> bind_rows() |> pivot_wider(names_from = tissue, values_from = n) write_csv(es_funnel, file.path(CSV_DIR, "deseq2", "effect_size_funnel.csv")) es_funnel ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: Candidates in an APOE-liver set (the full list, including genes outside every set, is in `csv/deseq2/effect_size_candidates.csv`): ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} es_genes |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(apoe_set)) |> dplyr::select(apoe_basis, apoe_set, Symbol, baseMean, log2FC, ci_lo, ci_hi, pvalue, padj, log2FC_oct, p_oct, dose_lfc_per_sd, p_dose, log2FC_germline_E2vsE4, log2FC_other_tissue, starts_with("ev_")) |> arrange(apoe_basis, apoe_set, pvalue) |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 2))) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: All other candidates (no APOE-liver set), by p value: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} es_genes |> dplyr::filter(is.na(apoe_set)) |> dplyr::select(Symbol, baseMean, log2FC, pvalue, padj, log2FC_oct, log2FC_germline_E2vsE4, log2FC_other_tissue, starts_with("ev_")) |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 2))) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ## Pathways **Pathways.** Two complementary views: 1. **APOE-liver sets.** GSEA of each set on the Wald statistic of every contrast that bears on the switch: main, 2025-10 only, within-Cre dose, germline E2 vs E4, and brain as the negative control. FDR is controlled within the small family (a priori / from this data), not across all of GO. Testing a few hypothesis-driven sets is the standard way to keep power, provided the sets are fixed before looking. 2. **Genome-wide GO near-misses.** Terms with |NES| ≥ 1.5 and 0.05 ≤ FDR < 0.25 in the main liver GSEA, with leave-one-out and 2025-10-only direction. Subramanian et al. (2005) recommend FDR < 0.25 for exploratory GSEA. Caveat: preranked GSEA permutes genes, not samples. It ignores correlation between genes, so its p values are optimistic for sets of co-regulated genes (Wu & Smyth 2012). Agreement across contrasts is a better guide than any single p value. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # 1. APOE-liver sets: GSEA on the Wald statistic (signed, scaled by uncertainty) of every contrast # that bears on the switch, so each set is read against the same lines of evidence as a gene. # FDR is controlled within each family (a priori / this data), not across all of GO: a small, # pre-specified family is the standard way to keep power for hypothesis-driven sets. set_t2g <- apoe_sets |> dplyr::select(set, genes) |> unnest(genes) |> dplyr::rename(gene = genes) stat_rank <- function(r) { s <- set_names(r$stat, rownames(r)) sort(s[!is.na(s)], decreasing = TRUE) } gsea_sets <- function(r, contrast) { g <- clusterProfiler::GSEA(stat_rank(r), TERM2GENE = set_t2g, pvalueCutoff = 1, minGSSize = 5, maxGSSize = 2000, eps = 0, seed = TRUE, verbose = FALSE) |> as.data.frame() tibble(set = g$ID, NES = g$NES, pvalue = g$pvalue, setSize = g$setSize, leading_edge = map_chr(str_split(g$core_enrichment, "/"), \(x) paste(na.omit(id2name$Symbol[match(x, id2name$ensemblID)]), collapse = "/")), contrast = contrast) } liver_fit <- fits$fit[[match("Liver", fits$tissue)]] germ_liver <- germline$res[[which(germline$tissue == "Liver" & germline$a == "E2" & germline$b == "E4")]] SET_CONTRASTS <- c("Cre vs GFP (main)", "Cre vs GFP (2025-10 only)", "Dose: E2 fraction (Cre only)", "Germline E2 vs E4", "Brain Cre vs GFP (neg. control)") set_gsea <- list(liver_fit$res, liver_fit$within, dose_gene_res("Liver"), germ_liver, fits$fit[[match("Brain", fits$tissue)]]$res) |> map2(SET_CONTRASTS, gsea_sets) |> bind_rows() |> left_join(dplyr::select(APOE_LIVER_SETS, set, basis), by = "set") |> group_by(contrast, basis) |> mutate(padj_family = p.adjust(pvalue, "BH")) |> ungroup() # leave-one-GFP-out for the main contrast: does the set keep its sign? set_loo <- imap(liver_fit$loo, \(l, k) gsea_sets(l$res, k)) |> bind_rows() |> group_by(set) |> summarise(loo_min_abs_NES = min(abs(NES)), loo_signs = list(sign(NES)), .groups = "drop") set_tbl <- set_gsea |> dplyr::filter(contrast == SET_CONTRASTS[1]) |> left_join(set_loo, by = "set") |> mutate(loo_same_sign = map2_lgl(loo_signs, NES, \(s, n) all(s == sign(n)))) |> dplyr::select(-loo_signs) |> left_join(set_gsea |> dplyr::filter(contrast != SET_CONTRASTS[1]) |> dplyr::select(set, contrast, NES) |> pivot_wider(names_from = contrast, values_from = NES, names_prefix = "NES: "), by = "set") write_csv(set_tbl, file.path(CSV_DIR, "pathway", "apoe_liver_sets_main_with_checks.csv")) write_csv(set_gsea, file.path(CSV_DIR, "pathway", "apoe_liver_sets_gsea_all_contrasts.csv")) set_tbl |> dplyr::select(basis, set, setSize, NES, pvalue, padj_family, loo_same_sign) |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 2))) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # 2. genome-wide GO near-misses: |NES| >= ES_NES and PADJ_CUT <= padj < ES_GSEA_FDR in the main # liver GSEA (same ranking as PATHWAY ANALYSIS: shrunk log2FC), with leave-one-out and 2025-10- # only direction. GSEA's authors recommend FDR < 0.25 for exploratory, hypothesis-generating use. near_miss <- map(c("BP", "MF", "CC"), \(o) { main <- gsea_all(lfc_table(liver_fit$res, liver_fit$resLFC$log2FoldChange), o) loo <- imap(liver_fit$loo, \(l, k) gsea_all(lfc_table(l$res, l$lfc), o) |> transmute(ID, NES_loo = NES, dropped = k)) |> bind_rows() w <- gsea_all(lfc_table(liver_fit$within, liver_fit$within$log2FoldChange), o) |> transmute(ID, NES_within = NES) main |> dplyr::filter(abs(NES) >= ES_NES, p.adjust >= PADJ_CUT, p.adjust < ES_GSEA_FDR) |> transmute(ont = o, ID, Description, setSize, NES, pvalue, p.adjust, leading_edge = map_chr(str_split(core_enrichment, "/"), \(x) paste(na.omit(suppressMessages(mapIds(org.Mm.eg.db, x, "SYMBOL", "ENTREZID"))), collapse = "/"))) |> left_join(loo |> group_by(ID) |> summarise(n_loo = n(), loo_same_sign_n = list(sign(NES_loo)), .groups = "drop"), by = "ID") |> left_join(w, by = "ID") |> mutate(loo_same_sign = map2_lgl(loo_same_sign_n, NES, \(s, n) length(s) == length(liver_fit$loo) && all(s == sign(n))), within_same_sign = sign(NES_within) == sign(NES)) |> dplyr::select(-loo_same_sign_n) }) |> bind_rows() |> arrange(p.adjust) write_csv(near_miss, file.path(CSV_DIR, "pathway", "liver_gseGO_near_miss.csv")) near_miss |> dplyr::count(ont, loo_same_sign, within_same_sign) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: GO near-misses (all three ontologies): ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} near_miss |> dplyr::select(ont, Description, setSize, NES, pvalue, p.adjust, loo_same_sign, within_same_sign, leading_edge) |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 2))) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ## Gene figures **Figures.** On each gene row: - black dot: main-model log2FC, with its 95% CI; - pink ring: 2025-10 only; - blue triangle: germline E2 vs E4; - grey cross: brain; - dashed lines: the ±1.5-fold threshold; - `*`: a gene in a set chosen from this data. The tiles on the right are the evidence columns. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} EV_COLS <- c(ev_nominal_main = "p < 0.05, main model", ev_nominal_oct = "p < 0.05, 2025-10 only", ev_dose_same_sign = "Dose: same sign", ev_dose_nominal = "Dose: p < 0.05", ev_germline_E2_like = "Germline E2 vs E4: same sign", ev_germline_nominal = "Germline: p < 0.05", ev_tissue_specific = "Liver-specific (brain < half)", ev_not_replicate_fp = "Not a replicate FP", ev_not_lib_quality = "Not tracking library quality") fig_genes <- function(d, show_other = TRUE, other_label = sprintf("Other (top %d by p)", ES_SHOW_OTHER)) { show <- bind_rows(dplyr::filter(d, !is.na(apoe_set)), if (show_other) d |> dplyr::filter(is.na(apoe_set)) |> slice_min(pvalue, n = ES_SHOW_OTHER, with_ties = FALSE)) |> mutate(group = factor(replace_na(apoe_set, other_label), levels = c(APOE_LIVER_SETS$set, other_label)) |> droplevels(), gene = fct_reorder(paste0(Symbol, ifelse(apoe_basis %in% "this data", "*", "")), log2FC)) pts <- show |> dplyr::select(group, gene, `Cre vs GFP (main)` = log2FC, `2025-10 only` = log2FC_oct, `Germline E2 vs E4` = log2FC_germline_E2vsE4, Brain = log2FC_other_tissue) |> pivot_longer(-c(group, gene), names_to = "estimate", values_to = "lfc") |> mutate(estimate = factor(estimate, levels = c("Cre vs GFP (main)", "2025-10 only", "Germline E2 vs E4", "Brain"))) lim <- 3 forest <- ggplot(show, aes(y = gene)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.25) + geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1) * ES_LFC, linewidth = 0.2, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") + geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = pmax(ci_lo, -lim), xmax = pmin(ci_hi, lim)), width = 0, linewidth = 0.3, orientation = "y") + geom_point(data = pts, aes(x = pmax(pmin(lfc, lim), -lim), shape = estimate, colour = estimate), size = 1, stroke = 0.4) + scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 1, 17, 4), name = NULL) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("black", GROUP_COLS[["Cre"]], "#2166AC", "grey55"), name = NULL) + facet_grid(group ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y", labeller = label_wrap_gen(20)) + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-lim, lim), oob = scales::squish) + labs(x = "log2 fold change (bar: main-model 95% CI)", y = NULL) + theme_bulk(6.5) + theme(strip.placement = "outside", strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 6), legend.position = "top", panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "mm"), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6, face = "italic")) tiles <- show |> dplyr::select(group, gene, all_of(names(EV_COLS))) |> pivot_longer(all_of(names(EV_COLS)), names_to = "check", values_to = "pass") |> mutate(check = factor(EV_COLS[check], levels = EV_COLS), pass = factor(case_when(is.na(pass) ~ "n/a", pass ~ "yes", TRUE ~ "no"), levels = c("yes", "no", "n/a"))) evid <- ggplot(tiles, aes(check, gene, fill = pass)) + geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) + facet_grid(group ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") + scale_fill_manual(values = c(yes = "grey20", no = "grey92", `n/a` = "white"), name = NULL) + scale_x_discrete(position = "top") + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_bulk(6.5) + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), axis.line = element_blank(), strip.text = element_blank(), panel.spacing = unit(0.6, "mm"), axis.text.x.top = element_text(size = 6, angle = 90, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5), legend.position = "top") list(plot = forest + evid + plot_layout(widths = c(1.25, 1)), n = nrow(show), n_groups = n_distinct(show$group)) } # two pages so each stays readable at print size: (1) a priori APOE-liver sets, (2) sets chosen from # this data + the top candidates outside every set gene_pages <- list(a_priori = dplyr::filter(es_genes, apoe_basis %in% "a priori"), this_data = dplyr::filter(es_genes, !apoe_basis %in% "a priori")) gene_figs <- imap(gene_pages, \(d, nm) { fg <- fig_genes(d, show_other = nm == "this_data") h <- min(240, 30 + 2.6 * fg$n + 1.5 * fg$n_groups) save_plot(fg$plot, file.path(FIG_DIR, "deseq2", paste0("effect_size_genes_liver_", nm)), "full", h) list(plot = fg$plot, height_in = h / 25.4) }) ``` ::: ### A priori APOE-liver sets ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](06-effect-size_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=657.637795275591} ::: ::: ### Sets chosen from this data, and the top candidates outside every set ::: {.cell} ::: factor(contrast, levels = SET_CONTRASTS), set = factor(set, levels = rev(APOE_LIVER_SETS$set)), basis = factor(basis, levels = c("a priori", "this data"), labels = c("A priori", "From this data")),
